thread.title: Fitbit: Time To Sell Again? - Fitbit, Inc. (NYSE:FIT)

author: Bill Maurer
title: Fitbit: Time To Sell Again? - Fitbit, Inc. (NYSE:FIT)
text:
One of this week's biggest winners so far is wearables company Fitbit ( FIT ). As seen in the chart below, shares have rallied almost 20% after the company announced its new smartwatch Versa is the fastest-selling product in the firm's history. While this news appears positive at first glance, a rally like this usually provides investors a good chance to exit.
( Source: Yahoo Finance)
Despite the Versa selling extremely well so far, management only reiterated revenue guidance for the year. While a Q2 beat may come, the second half of the year is where things get really interesting if we take a look at current analyst estimates . Revenues declined by 17% in Q1 and are forecast to drop 19% in Q2, yet for the whole year, the Street only expects a decline of 9%.
That means comparisons for the second half of 2018 are a lot tougher. With the company seeing very soft sales for its traditional trackers, will the Versa be able to continue this momentum for the rest of the year or was this just a strong initial sales push? Even with some early sales in March from the Versa, IDC showed below how Fitbit lost a significant chunk of market share over the prior-year period.
( Source: IDC Q1 2018 wearables report )
Also, don't forget the sandbox that Fitbit is currently trying to play in. While a million watches in about two months sounds good, don't forget that Apple ( AAPL ) is selling a few times that per quarter and at a significantly higher price point. As I've discussed previously, Apple could destroy Fitbit if it wanted to because the tech giant's quarterly Watch revenues at this point are about as much as Fitbit does in an entire year. After four new countries got the LTE variant of the Watch 3 last month, four more are starting pre-orders this week. The fourth generation is expected to feature a larger display as well as longer battery life, and that could come as early as this fall.
The other major problem for Fitbit's 2018 is the expected launch of the Pixel Watch from Alphabet/Google ( GOOG ) ( GOOGL ). Fitbit is having enough of a problem battling Apple, so the entrance of a second tech giant only makes the situation worse when you have other competitors like Garmin ( GRMN ). Even sales of a few hundred thousand Pixel Watches could easily cause Fitbit to miss estimates, especially when you are facing tougher comps in 2H 2018.
The other part of the problem is that Fitbit's balance sheet is weakening a little. The company burned through $25 million in cash last year, and free cash flow is expected to decline again this year when excluding the benefit of a large tax refund payment. Significant GAAP losses are not helping the situation, gross margins are declining thanks to more revenues coming from smartwatches, and operating expenses aren't coming down fast enough. Management also upped its capex forecast at the Q1 report.
In the end, the recent rally from Fitbit may be another chance to sell. Versa sales may have had a good two months, but management only held guidance steady and second half comps are tougher than first half. It will be hard for the company to keep sales momentum going as Apple Watch sales continue to excel and Google enters the space. With soft margins leading to more losses and cash burn, it's a tough industry for Fitbit to be in, unless you are counting on a buyout to occur. Shares have rallied like this before only to come back down, which could easily happen again.
